harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured `inventory-worker` on node1 as an enabled systemd service running under dedicated account `inventorysvc`. It is confined to the root-owned `/srv/inventory-chroot`, with `/var/lib/inventory` as its only writable application directory. Configuration, service, and data survived a verified node reboot without changing Ubuntu 16.04 or kernel 4.4.0-210.
actions_performed: Created system account `inventorysvc` with UID/GID 999 and a non-login shell.
Built a minimal legacy-compatible chroot using the existing statically linked BusyBox.
Created and enabled `inventory-worker.service` with `RootDirectory`, `User`, `Group`, `NoNewPrivileges`, and no capabilities.
Verified denied writes throughout the chroot except `/var/lib/inventory`.
Restarted node1 safely and confirmed boot identity, service, confinement, and application-data recovery.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated unprivileged background worker managed as inventory-worker
evidence.summary: Shows the dedicated account, enabled and active service, UID/GID 999 processes, and generated heartbeat data.

evidence.requirement: Root-owned chroot with /var/lib/inventory as the only writable application directory
evidence.summary: Proves the live process root and cwd, zero capabilities, root ownership outside the data subtree, denied write probes elsewhere, and successful writing only under `/var/lib/inventory`.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed legacy OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 16.04 and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic were observed before configuration, before reboot, and after reboot.

Captures healthy baseline boot ID `2dffe735-a982-49f0-aa0a-19552507ae73`, reboot acknowledgement, new boot ID `6dd16786-f4fd-400a-8157-153173308ba9`, and recovered service, confinement, heartbeat, and unchanged persistence-probe hash.
